'''Marius Lacombe''' (7 February 1862 – 19 March 1938) was a Swiss [[mathematician]].

== Life and work ==
Lacombe studied mathematics at Engineers Department of the [[ETH Zurich]].{{sfn | Eminger | 2015 | p=123 }} From 1890 to 1894 he was teaching [[descriptive geometry]] in the [[university of Lausanne]].{{sfn | Khouyibaba | 1997 | p=42 }} In 1894 he was appointed professor at ETH Zurich{{sfn | Frei | Stammbach | 1994 | p=46 }} to fill a newly created chair of descriptive geometry in French language.{{sfn | Oswald | Volkert | 2018 | p=29 }} After fourteen years in Zurich, in 1908 he returned to university of Lausane, where he retired in 1927.{{sfn | Khouyibaba | 1997 | p=43 }}

He was more a teacher than a researcher. His only known works deal on pedagogy of mathematics.{{sfn | Eminger | 2015 | p=124-125 }}{{sfn | Khouyibaba | 1997 | p=43 }} In 1896 he was one of the organizers of the first International Congress of Mathematicians.
